requirement: Breast and melanoma studies associate organised immune responses with outcomes, retaining each study's specimens, methods and setting.
supportingExcerpt: In untreated invasive breast-tumour specimens, Gu-Trantien and colleagues linked CXCL13-producing follicular helper T cells in TLS germinal centres and an eight-gene signature to group outcomes, including survival or preoperative chemotherapy response. In metastatic melanoma samples, Cabrita and colleagues associated co-occurring CD8-positive T cells and CD20-positive B cells with survival, and a derived TLS signature predicted outcomes in checkpoint-blockade cohorts. Each result retains its specimens, methods and setting; these associations do not establish that inducing a TLS will benefit a particular patient.
